references.text: The camp of Israel in the plains of Moab by the Jordan, opposite Jericho, is also mentioned here as the place where the Balak story begins.
Shittim (Abel-Shittim) is the place where the Israelites sinned with Moabite women and began to worship Baal-Peor.
The plains of Moab by the Jordan, opposite Jericho, are mentioned as the campsite where the spoils from the Midianites were brought.
The plains of Moab by the Jordan, opposite Jericho, is the place where the Lord spoke to Moses about the Levitical cities.
The plains of Moab by the Jordan, opposite Jericho, are mentioned as the place where commands and laws were given through Moses.
The plains of Moab is the area where Moses went up Mount Nebo to see the promised land before he died.
Joshua sent spies from Shittim to Jericho, showing that this was the Israelites' last campsite before they crossed the Jordan.
Joshua and the Israelites broke camp from Shittim and came to the Jordan before crossing over into the promised land.
Beth-jeshimoth is mentioned as part of King Sihon's territory that the Israelites conquered.
The prophet Micah reminds the people of what happened from Shittim to Gilgal, referring to the crossing of the Jordan.
